term: Our fabled shores none ever reach
note: A line from Henry David Thoreau’s poem “The Atlantides,” which imagines friendship through the image of elusive, unexplored islands.

short: James Thomson, author of The Seasons.
note: The Scottish poet James Thomson (1700–1748), whose long poem The Seasons includes the stormy northern-island passage in its section “Autumn.”

short: The Greek-language satirist of True History.
note: A second-century satirist from Samosata. His True History parodies extravagant travel writing with impossible voyages, including a journey to the Moon.

sources.label: Lucian: True History and other works

short: The legendary island associated with King Arthur.
note: The island to which Arthur is taken after his final battle in medieval romance. Glastonbury became associated with Avalon; its monks claimed in 1191 to have found Arthur’s grave.

sources.label: Glastonbury Abbey: King Arthur and Avalon

note: Hy-Brasil, a legendary island west of Ireland, said to appear only once every seven years. It remained on European maps for centuries despite never being found.

short: The enigmatic host in John Fowles’s The Magus.
note: Maurice Conchis, the wealthy recluse who conducts elaborate psychological performances on the Greek island of Phraxos in John Fowles’s The Magus (1965).

short: A passage from Kazantzakis’s Zorba the Greek.
note: A passage from Nikos Kazantzakis’s Zorba the Greek (1946), celebrating travel among the Aegean islands.

sources.label: Bloomsbury preview: Harry Mount quotes Zorba the Greek

note: A line from Alfred, Lord Tennyson’s “Ulysses,” in which the aging voyager urges his companions toward one more journey beyond the known world.

short: Small islands in rivers or lakes.
note: Small islands, especially within rivers; also spelled aits.

short: Small islands or low river meadows.
note: An older northern English and Scots term for small islands, also used for low-lying land beside water.
The Latin noun insula means island, whether in the sea, a river, or a lake.
The adventuring prince from Thule in Hal Foster’s comic strip, first published in 1937 and set in the age of King Arthur.

short: The sacred Greek island of Apollo and Artemis.
note: A small Cycladic island honored as the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis in Greek mythology and the site of a major sanctuary of Apollo.

short: The Aegean island associated with Revelation.
note: The Greek island named in Revelation 1:9 as John’s place of exile, traditionally associated with his visions of the Apocalypse.

sources.label: UNESCO: Patmos and the Cave of the Apocalypse

note: The island society described in Thomas More’s Utopia (1516), a political fiction examining property, government, religion, and social organization.

short: The fictional Greek island in Fowles’s The Magus.
note: The Greek island setting of John Fowles’s The Magus, where the young English teacher Nicholas Urfe encounters the wealthy Maurice Conchis.
